properties.name: Battle of Thermopylae (480 BC)
properties.location: Pass of Thermopylae, Anthele / Kolonos Hill, Greece
properties.description: Spartan King Leonidas and 7,000 allied Greeks deployed the dense hoplite phalanx in the narrow coastal pass to bottle up and defeat repeated frontal assaults by Xerxes I's Persian imperial army.
properties.tactical_feature: Chokepoint bottlenecking, overlapping aspis bronze shields, othismos forward mass.

properties.name: Battle of Hastings (1066)
properties.location: Senlac Hill / Battle Abbey, Battle, East Sussex, England, UK
properties.description: King Harold II Godwinson arrayed the Anglo-Saxon army in a dense, interlocking shield wall along Senlac Hill, repelling hours of Norman cavalry and infantry assaults until broken by feigned retreats.
properties.tactical_feature: Elevated ridge defense, interlocking linden-wood shields with iron bosses, Dane axe front-rank shock counter.

properties.name: Battle of Carrhae (53 BC)
properties.description: Marcus Licinius Crassus's Roman legions formed dense shield arrays against Parthian horse archers, only to be charged and trampled by heavily armored cataphracts in open desert terrain.
properties.tactical_feature: Catastrophic dilemma: locked shields vulnerable to cataphract shock, loosened ranks vulnerable to arrow swarms.

properties.name: Siege of Cremona (69 AD)
properties.description: Flavian legions under Marcus Antonius Primus advanced under the city ramparts in tight testudo formation to deflect catapult missiles, stones, and darts while attacking the fortifications.
properties.tactical_feature: Curved scuta locked overhead and on flanks, deflecting plunging missile barrages during assault.

properties.name: Siege of Jerusalem (70 AD)
properties.description: Titus's Roman legions utilized the testudo formation to protect legionary engineers and sappers undermining city ramparts and breaching the Antonia Fortress.
properties.tactical_feature: Shield roof providing mobile ballistic armor for breaching teams and battering rams.

properties.name: Battle of Verdun - Mémorial de Verdun (1916)
properties.location: Fleury-devant-Douaumont, Verdun, Meuse, Grand Est, France
properties.description: The epic 302-day battle exemplifying industrial defense-in-depth, where echeloned trenches, machine gun crossfires, and massive artillery barrages absorbed Falkenhayn's attrition offensive.
properties.tactical_feature: Traversed fire trenches, barbed wire kill zones, subterranean dugouts, Noria unit rotation system.

properties.name: Fort de Douaumont - Verdun (1916)
properties.description: The central high-ground subterranean armored fortress of the Fortified Region of Verdun, anchor of the Meuse Heights defensive network.
properties.tactical_feature: Reinforced concrete underground galleries, 155mm retractable armored turrets, fortified redoubts.
